key_insight: Stronger shear and rotation intensify secondary circulation, enhancing heat transfer and producing thinner, more radially uneven equilibrium ice.
engineering_relevance: The findings could improve predictions of ice evolution in meandering rivers, informing flood-risk assessment and winter transportation planning.
method: Combine experiments, numerical simulations, and theory in an annular ice–water system.
Model mean ice thickness using an integral thermal balance.
Relate inner–outer thickness differences to nonuniform convective heat flux using a local thermal balance.
evidence_signal: Annular experiments and simulations support the proposed mechanism, while the local model shows qualitative agreement with field measurements from an ice-covered meandering river.
watch_item: Field agreement is qualitative; predictive accuracy in natural rivers with more complex geometry and thermal forcing remains to be established.
